quarterly_data.quarter: Rockwell Automation Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: End-market mix and growth framework (CEO Blake Moret): automotive is about 10% of Rockwell's total business (low double-digit growth last quarter); process is 'all in 40%' of total business, with discrete about 25%; home and personal care grew high single digits in the last quarter. The growth algorithm is an all-in 6%-9% top-line target CAGR through the cycle, with 3%-5% of that being market growth including price and 1%-2% from expanding markets (mobile robots, FactoryTalk Optix, digital twin creation) and share growth. Content per unit of customer capex is 'still too variable by individual industry' to give a percentage: a new automobile assembly line within an existing building carries significantly higher Rockwell content than a $10 billion wafer fab, where Rockwell's content is 'a fraction of 1%'. CEO: the underlying customer tone is 'distinctly positive' and North America is 'the best place to be investing now', but there is still no 'wholesale release of CapEx'; a reduction in trade uncertainty with Canada and Mexico, particularly in automotive, would release more capital.
quarterly_data.figure: automotive about 10% of total business; process all in 40%, discrete about 25%; target CAGR 6%-9% through the cycle (3%-5% market growth, 1%-2% expanding markets and share growth); wafer fab content a fraction of 1%

quarterly_data.quarter: Rockwell Automation Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor (CEO Blake Moret): semiconductor and new fabs have been one of Rockwell's top one or two industries in Asia 'for a very long time' (facilities management and control systems), and a US semiconductor facility was 'one of the largest Logix installations in the world'. Newer offerings include work with chiller OEMs and, at one of Texas Instruments' fabs, optimizing its chillers using AI and wafer transport with Rockwell's independent cart technology - capabilities Rockwell did not have 10 or 15 years ago.

quarterly_data.quarter: Rockwell Automation Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Own capacity and margins (CEO Blake Moret): Rockwell recently announced a major new plant very close to its Wisconsin headquarters; the first products will not come out of that plant until 2028. Investments of roughly $2 billion in plants, talent and digital infrastructure aim largely at 'that next tier of margin increases' and improved customer service. Rockwell has roughly doubled the profitability of its LifecycleIQ Services business in a relatively short period ('We're not done'), is committed to expanding margins 'going to and through historic levels', and after the 2024 / early-2025 reductions in force is still down almost 10% in headcount from its peak in early 2024, adding resources with discipline and AI tools while keeping its percentage investment in engineering and development. Intelligent Devices (Tessa Myers): margin levers are volume, direct material costs (commercial negotiations, product redesign, alternative components), manufacturing efficiency and logistics.
quarterly_data.figure: new Wisconsin plant first products 2028; roughly $2 billion invested in plants, talent and digital infrastructure; headcount down almost 10% from early-2024 peak

quarterly_data.quarter: Rockwell Automation Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor and memory supply (CEO Blake Moret): 'I think we can stay ahead of it in terms of price.' Rockwell has 'a certain amount of long-term supply agreements with the semiconductor suppliers' but is not counting on any near-term moderation of the pace of increases, 'particularly in memory'; it 'did a nice job of buying ahead', holds inventory in tranches of differently costed components and is using more frequent price increases expected to keep up with cost and preserve margin. 'We are not seeing that affect availability of the memory': compared with data-center demand Rockwell and its peers are relatively small consumers and 'are still getting the supply that we need, albeit at a very inflationary price.' Tessa Myers (Intelligent Devices): the company can evaluate alternates and design in alternate vendors; CEO: development engineers are also shifting suppliers from high-risk areas and factoring in inflation from data-center demand.

quarterly_data.quarter: Rockwell Automation Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Competitive position (CEO Blake Moret): recently released market share reports 'look good' and support the company's view that 'we are taking modest share in some really important places'. European end-of-line packaging machine builders are increasing their North American capacity, and with Rockwell's new products 'we are winning more than our fair share' with them. Rockwell has 'a mobile robot that none of our major competitors have', fleet management for its mobile robots that can be extended to other types of robots including humanoids, and a system-wide software-defined automation offering (virtual PLC, simulation tools, agents, FactoryTalk Optix at the edge). Tessa Myers: several new product introductions are 'growing beyond our expectations', winning new customers and share, not only existing customers.
